items.headline: Advisory committee to review City Hall's condition and future options
items.summary: The City Hall Community Advisory Committee is scheduled to meet November 16 for discussion and input on City Hall's existing conditions, facility needs, and future options. The agenda also lists approval of minutes from the committee's October 29 meeting.

items.headline: Council committee to take up gift rules for city officials
items.summary: The Governance and Ethics Committee is scheduled to consider proposed updates to Council Policy 050, which covers gifts to elected and appointed officials. It will also take up changes to Council Policy 030, on how items get added to council agendas, which were deferred from its June 1 meeting.

items.headline: Campbell planners listed rezoning of 480 Chapman from commercial to single-family
items.summary: The November 10 Planning Commission agenda listed a public hearing on a request to change a single-family home at 480 Chapman from Neighborhood Commercial to Low Density Residential and R-1-10 zoning, which would end its legal nonconforming status. Staff recommended the commission send the amendments to the City Council, tentatively scheduled for December 1, 2026.

items.headline: Planning Commission agenda: 251 affordable-housing units at 10333 N. Wolfe Road
items.summary: The November 10 agenda listed Eden Housing's request for Architectural and Site Approval and Tree Removal Permits for a 251-unit residential development with trail improvements at 10333 N. Wolfe Road. The project would remove and replace 117 protected trees.

items.headline: Planning Commission agenda: 363 apartments proposed on Stevens Creek Boulevard office site
items.summary: The November 10 agenda listed The Hanover Company's proposal for a 363-unit apartment development at 19220-19300 Stevens Creek Boulevard, replacing existing office buildings. The project is on Sites 5 and 6 of the city's priority housing sites and uses SB 330 and State Density Bonus law.

items.headline: Eight-story, 200-unit rental building pitched for 720 San Antonio Road
items.summary: The November 9 City Council agenda listed a prescreening request to rezone the 1.35-acre site at 720 San Antonio Road from Service Commercial to Planned Community/Planned Home zoning. The proposal would allow 200 rental units in an eight-story building. The same agenda listed a review of 60% design plans for the Quarry Road Transit Connection.

items.headline: Washington Street lot listed as historic eyed for 1,200 sq ft ADU
items.summary: The Historical and Landmarks Commission's November 5 agenda listed a public hearing on a recommendation for a 1,200-square-foot detached accessory dwelling unit and a 347-square-foot detached garage at 1391 Washington Street (PLN26-00020). The property is on the city's Historic Resource Inventory, so the alteration needs historic review. The project is listed as categorically exempt from CEQA.

items.headline: Landmarks commission to pick member for preservation ordinance consultant panel
items.summary: The November 5 Historical and Landmarks Commission agenda listed the selection of one commissioner to serve on the review board choosing a consultant for the Historic Preservation Ordinance update. The update would revise the city's rules for protecting historic buildings.
